key_insight: Accurate macroscopic shock profiles do not guarantee accurate fourth-order kinetic closure, because the hard-to-observe tail-weighted moments can still carry large errors.
engineering_relevance: For kinetic shock solvers, this means training must target the right moment projections or closure errors in heat transfer and stress predictions may persist even when density, velocity, and temperature look correct.
method: Positive macro–micro PINN with a bounded exponential correction to represent the distribution
Sparse joint anchoring of heat flux and normal stress to stabilize the nonequilibrium shock layer
Shock-local closure correction aligned with the missing tail-weighted projection
evidence_signal: Against discrete-velocity references, the flux-locked model matched lower moments and $m_{xxx}^{cl}$ but left $R_{xx}^{cl}$ at order-unity error, which was reduced to $1.12\times10^{-1}$ after the tailored closure correction.
watch_item: The optional distribution-function probe losses appear diagnostic rather than constitutive, so relying on them as a training requirement may not improve the underlying closure observability.
paper_title: Tail observability and fourth-order closure recovery in physics-informed neural networks for Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook normal shocks
